rules.name: Assault
rules.text: This weapon suffers no penalty 'to hit' when moving and shooting. In addition, infantry models armed with an assault weapon count as having the Tough Fighters special rule (Tough Fighters: When a model with this special rule fails to damage in close quarters against enemy infantry or artillery units, it can re-roll the failed rolls to damage)

rules.name: Bicycles
rules.text: When moving on roads, they double their Run move to 24" (cannot be used to Assault). The first time they receive any order other than Run, or if they receive a Pin marker, they dismount and abandon their bicycles for the rest of the game.

rules.name: Cavalry
rules.text: Can dismount and fight on foot as infantry, from which point none of these rules apply - need to replace mounted figures with non-mounted figures. When cavalry, moves 9" at an Advance, 18" at Run. Cannot enter buildings or board transport vehicles unless they have dismounted. Cannot gain advantages of Down, and their cover saves are always reduced by 1. Can escape as a recce vehicle (at normal speed, not double speed). Can dismount as part of Advance move - cannot remount. Can only fire pistol or carbine (treated as pistol) when mounted. While mounted, cavalry have Tough Fighters special rule (p122- When fails to damage in close quarters against enemy infantry or artillery units, it can re-roll the failed rolls to damage). Can regroup up to 2D6" after combat.

rules.name: Motorbikes
rules.text: Moves at 12" at an Advance and 24" at a Run with the same movement rules and restrictions as Wheeled vehicles, except they may make any number of turns as they move. Cannot enter builders or board transports. Do not benefit from any advantage from going/being Down. Can react by making and escape move in the same way as recce (at normal move, not double speed). Can dismount as part of any Advance move and fight as infantry, but cannot remount. Motorcycle riders cannot shoot while moving. Cannot assault and if assaulted can make an escape move as for other recce vehicles. If attacked at close quarters each man fights as infantry (including sidecar passengers if equipped). Regroup 2D6" rather than D6".

rules.name: Tough Fighters
rules.text: When a model with this special rule fails to damage in close quarters against enemy infantry or artillery units, it can re-roll the failed rolls to damage.

armyRules.name: Death Before Dishonour
armyRules.text: All Imperial Japanese infantry and artillery units have the Fanatics special rule. In addition, they automatically pass morale checks for being assaulted by enemy tanks (note that artillery pieces are still destroyed as normal).

armyRules.name: Banzai!
armyRules.text: A Japanese Officer may be given a special Banzai! order. This counts as a "You Men Snap to Action" with the following exceptions: If the order is given successfully, assign the officer a Run order die. Then

armyRules.name: ALL
armyRules.text: infantry units within 6” that haven’t already received an order that turn are issued a Run order. Note that this includes infantry units which cannot normally assault enemies, such as those with the Fixed special rule, or the Self-defence special rule. All infantry units can and will assault into close quarters if given the opportunity (09/2026 errata). Note that, other than for the initiating officer, no order test is required for any units affected by a Banzai! order. This means that affected units execute their Run orders automatically, without any dice rolled, and as such retain any pin markers they have.

armyRules.name: Lack of Radios
armyRules.text: When you give the Command Vehicle special rule to a vehicle that does not have it in its entry for the purposes of choosing a command vehicle for an Armoured Platoon, you can give it the rule for free instead of paying the normal +10pts. If you do so, the vehicle reduces the radius of its Command Vehicle rule from 12” to 6”. This represents communication by means of flags or hand signals.

rules.name: Engineers
rules.text: When a unit of engineers assaults a building, the defenders cannot benefit from the defensive position bonus (see apge 110). In addition (page 296, 297): Engineering units attempting to cut barbed wire are automatically successful, but still require a Down order to do so. Combat engineers can clear an adjacent anti-tank ditch by receiving a Down order, but not as a reaction to enemy fire. Always benefit from re-roll when moving at an Advance even when crossing the enemy's minefields. Engineers receive +1 to clearing minefields (page 299).

rules.name: HE (1")
rules.text: PEN: +1, PIN: D2 (D3 if in building) - Infantry and artillery can go down to halve the hits taken (rounded up).

rules.name: Indirect fire
rules.text: - cannot hit targets within their minimum range, measured from the centre the weapon itself. Units hit by indirect file receive no cover saves of any kind. However, if the target unit is or goes Down when shot at with indirect fire, the number of hits suffered is still halved. When fired against vehicles, hits from indirect fire weapons always strike the top armour, counting the +1 penetration modifier to damage regardless of the actual position of the firer. If an open-topped armoured vehicle is hit by indirect fire add the +1 penetration modifier to the roll to damage, and also add +1 to the die roll on the Armoured Vehicle Damage Results Tables. Cannot fire indirect fire weapons from Ambush. Indirect fire weapons can fire smoke (page 128).

rules.name: Tank hunters
rules.text: If a tank hunter unit wins an assault and scores damage against an armoured vehicle, the effect is resolved on the Damage Result table as for a normal anti-tank penetration rather than as for superficial damage. In addition, these troops don't suffer from the Tank Fear rule when assaulting fully-enclosed armoured vehicles.

rules.name: Flamethrower
rules.text: Hits from flamethowers allow no cover saves. When shooting with a flamethrower, roll a single die to hit as normal, but if you score a hit, it is turned into D6 hits (or D6+1 in the case of a vehicle-mounted flamethrower). As no saves are allowed, simply roll for damaage in the usual manner. Flamethrowers always hit the top armour of vehicles. Also, they don't suffer the -1 Pen penalty when firing at long range against armoured vehicles, nor the +1 Pen for firing at point-blank range. Causes D3+1 pins to target, 1 pin to firing unit. A unit hit by a flamethrower must check its morale regardless of casualties. After shooting roll a D6 (for each flamethrower fired). On a result of 1 or 2 the flamethrower has run out of fuel. Infantry: replace model with unarmed model, else remove the model instead (no morale check caused). Vehicles: no other effects. When rolling on Vehicle Damage Results table against a vehicle equipped with flamethrowers, add an extra +1 to the roll.

In addition, these troops don't suffer from the Tank Fear rule when assaulting fully-enclosed armoured vehicles.

rules.name: Team (2 men)

rules.name: Flak
rules.text: All enemy with the Flak special rule automatically fire at the attacking aircraft if the token model lies within their range and firing arc, regardless of whether they have already taken an action or not that turn. Flak fire does not require an action and takes place outside of the normal turn sequence. Firing a pintle-mounted machine gun flak weapon against an attacking aircraft does not make the vehicle count as open-topped for the turn. Any flak units in Ambush retain their Ambush status if they shoot at an aircraft. Hidden lose their hidden status. Friendly units must test to hold their fire (Inexperienced 4+, Regular 3+, Veteran 2+) - in case of Rookie pilot all flak units open fire automatically. Measure range - Line of Site ignored. Flak weapons not pinned hit on 5+, pinner hit on 6 - ignore all other modifiers. If HE hits, multiply as for inside a building. If 3 or more hits, shot down.
